title: Annual Estate Plan Review
description: A once-a-year check to confirm your documents, beneficiaries, and key people still match your life and wishes.
intro: An estate plan works best when it reflects your life today. Set aside an hour each year to walk through this list. If anything has changed, note it and decide whether to talk with your attorney.

sections.heading: Life changes this year
items: Marriage, divorce, or a new partner
Birth or adoption of a child or grandchild
Death or serious illness of a family member or someone named in your plan
Move to a new state
Change in a beneficiary's needs, such as a disability or money trouble
New business, retirement, or major job change

sections.heading: Money and property
items: New real estate purchased or sold
New bank, investment, or retirement accounts opened
Large change in the value of your estate
New debts or loans to family
New assets titled in the trust's name, if you have a trust

sections.heading: People in your plan
items: Confirm your executor and trustee are still willing and able
Confirm your financial and health care agents are still the right choice
Confirm your guardian choice for minor children still fits
Update contact information for everyone named

sections.heading: Documents and forms
items: Request current beneficiary designations on retirement accounts and insurance
Review your health care wishes and living will
Update your asset inventory and digital assets list
Update your letter of instruction
Confirm originals are stored safely and your executor knows where

sections.heading: Next steps
items: Write down any changes you want to make
Schedule a review with your attorney if anything significant changed
Set a reminder for next year's review
Use the plan review reminder tool to get a yearly prompt
